task: Research Peloton (onepeloton.com) for a hedge fund

key.question: What did Peloton report for Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended Sep 30, 2026, reported Nov 5, 2026) against guidance, and what is the quality of the beat?
key.answer: Revenue was $559M, up 2% year over year and about $4M above the guidance midpoint. This was the third straight quarter of year-over-year growth. Adjusted EBITDA was $168M (+42%), free cash flow was $143M, and gross margin was 61.3%. About $25M of the margin benefit was non-recurring, from tariff favorability and lower recall costs. Excluding those items, Connected Fitness gross margin was about 17%, versus about 33% reported. Ending paid Connected Fitness subscriptions were 2.475M, down 9% year over year and at the top of the guidance range. Q1 average net monthly churn was 1.7%. Net income is reported as about $96M, but sources differ slightly.

key.question: What is the current guidance (Q2 and full-year FY2027), and how does it compare with the Q1 run-rate?
key.answer: Q2 FY27 guidance: revenue $625–650M (about -3% year over year at the midpoint), adjusted EBITDA $85–100M, ending paid Connected Fitness subscriptions 2.425–2.445M (about -8.5%), and gross margin of about 50%. The full-year FY27 outlook was maintained: revenue $2.3–2.4B (about -4% at the midpoint), adjusted EBITDA $475–525M, gross margin of about 54%, and free cash flow of at least $350M. Full-year net churn is expected to be flat versus FY26. Management expects churn to improve meaningfully in Q2 as the October 2025 price increase starts to be lapped. The Q1 margin was inflated, so the guide implies a sharp step-down in the remaining quarters. Consensus figures were not verified.

key.question: What is Peloton's debt, liquidity and refinancing position, and when are the maturities?
key.answer: Peloton prepaid $280M of its term loan on Oct 9, 2026, cutting it to about $700M from nearly $1B. About $200M of 2026 notes were repaid at maturity in February 2026. Gross debt fell by about one-third in calendar 2026. Cash was $1.34B at quarter end, which exceeds total debt and gives a net cash position. The remaining stack is the term loan (from the May 2024 refinancing, five-year, with early-refinancing penalty protection) and the 5.50% convertible senior notes due Dec 1, 2029 (not redeemable before Jun 7, 2027). Management says there are no near-term maturities and it is being patient on any refinancing because of credit market volatility. Rating actions were not verified, so check S&P and Moody's.

key.question: What are the upcoming dated catalysts over the next 6 months?
key.answer: Q2 FY27 earnings, covering the holiday quarter, are expected in early February 2027. The date should be confirmed on the Peloton IR site. Q2 is guided to revenue of $625–650M and EBITDA of $85–100M. The Q2 subscriber guide and churn improvement as the October 2025 price increase is lapped are the key metrics to watch. The Tread lineup launched in the fall (Tread Flex at about $2,000, Tread Vision, Commercial Series). Peloton IQ updates launched Oct 1. A hardware launch in a new category is planned for fall 2027, which is outside the 6-month window. The convertible notes become redeemable from Jun 7, 2027, also outside the window.

key.question: Is there any M&A, activist, buyback or strategic review activity?
key.answer: No buyback has been announced. The CFO said any return of capital would be assessed with the Board with dilution in mind. The call transcript mentioned no strategic review, restructuring or layoffs. Management cited ongoing cost discipline, with G&A and R&D down about $14M year over year. The strategy under CEO Peter Stern is a shift to a connected wellness ecosystem. No activist 13D was found in my search, though that search was not exhaustive. Re-check EDGAR for 13D filings.

key.question: What do insider and 13D/G filings show?
key.answer: Many Form 4 filings were made in 2026, with the latest visible in September 2026, but my search did not retrieve the transaction details, so net insider buying or selling is unverified and should be pulled from EDGAR. The 13G filers found are Nantahala Capital at about 7.3% (May 2026), DNB Asset Management at about 6.6% (May 2026), and Vanguard Capital Management at 5.15% (21.1M shares, as of Mar 31, 2026). Vanguard Group filed a 13G/A showing 0 shares after a January 2026 internal realignment. FMR is at about 0.7% and T. Rowe Price at about 2.2%. These figures come from a third-party tracker, so verify them against the SEC filings.

key.question: What are the main risks to the thesis?
key.answer: (1) Paid Connected Fitness subscribers are shrinking about 9% year over year, with the guide at 2.425–2.445M for Q2. (2) Q1 margins were flattered by about $25M of tariff and recall benefits and will normalise, since Q2 gross margin is guided to about 50% and full-year to about 54%. (3) The full-year revenue guide implies a roughly 4% decline, so the growth in Q1 is not durable. (4) Churn relief depends on lapping the October 2025 price increase. (5) Tariff exposure persists, although suppliers have been diversified. (6) Capital allocation and dilution risk remain unresolved, and the term loan is about $700M. (7) The stock traded around $5.7 after the print, so check for a negative reaction.

key.question: Who leads the company and what is the strategy?
key.answer: Peter Stern is CEO. The strategy is cost discipline, deleveraging, supplier diversification for cheaper hardware (a treadmill about $1,000 below the prior base model), the Tread relaunch, commercial/Precor expansion, and a move into a connected wellness ecosystem with a new-category hardware launch in fall 2027. The CFO is assessing capital return together with the Board.
